subtitle: Confirming what you already know still works

code:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  order_date,
  order_total,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn,
  RANK()       OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_total DESC) AS total_rank,
  LAG(order_total)  OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS prev_total,
  LEAD(order_total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS next_total
FROM orders;
caption: Same names, same OVER() syntax — paste it straight from T-SQL.

code:
-- T-SQL: RECURSIVE is inferred
WITH org_chart AS ( ... )

-- Snowflake: RECURSIVE is required
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
  SELECT employee_id, manager_id, 1 AS level
  FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.employee_id, e.manager_id, oc.level + 1
  FROM employees e JOIN org_chart oc ON e.manager_id = oc.employee_id
)
SELECT * FROM org_chart;
caption: Forget RECURSIVE and Snowflake throws a syntax error, not a silent non-recursive query.

code:
-- Same result as CTE + WHERE rn = 1, in one query
SELECT customer_id, order_date, order_total,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn
FROM orders
QUALIFY rn = 1;
caption: Both patterns are correct — QUALIFY is just the Snowflake-only shortcut.
